plan: Store the deep-copied input dict as the single mutable tree; to_data() returns a fresh deep copy.
Implement one recursive generator that yields (item, nesting level) over the whole tree, recursing into section/group items.
Compute total_word_count by summing per-item contributions: notes count \b\w+\b runs after stripping [[?identifier]] markers; references contribute their declared word_count.
Collect unresolved markers into a set from note-text marker identifiers and reference unresolved lists, returning them sorted.
Render the outline as the workspace title plus one line per walked item with two spaces per level and '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move as validate-then-mutate: check string ids, locate item and destination, require a container destination ('workspace' or section/group), reject destinations inside the moving subtree via a subtree-id set, bounds-check the insertion index, and only then pop and insert.
mechanisms: Composite tree of dict nodes with sections/groups as containers and notes/references as leaves
Single recursive depth-first walker shared by all read operations
Recursive aggregation of word counts with kind-specific leaf contributions
Regex marker extraction and stripping for note text
Deterministic depth-first outline rendering with level-based indentation
Subtree-id-set containment check preventing self/descendant destinations
Validate-before-mutate move giving all-or-nothing failure semantics
Deep-copy isolation on construction and export

trace.target_mechanism: Composite tree of dict nodes where sections and groups contain further items and notes/references are leaves
One shared recursive walker driving word count, marker collection, and outline identically at every nesting depth
total_word_count and unresolved_markers accumulate leaf contributions over the full recursive walk
Depth-first, list-order traversal producing the indented outline deterministically
Container-kind check plus subtree-id-set test rejecting moves into non-containers, the item itself, or its descendants
All move validations complete before the pop/insert mutation, so any failure leaves to_data() unchanged
